title: Freeness on normalized abelian-level branches of a stable deformation
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, let $g\geq2$, and let $C/\Omega$ be a stable unpointed genus-$g$ curve with $d$ nodes. Let $\ell\geq3$ be prime and invertible in $\Omega$. Stable curves, the smooth moduli groupoid $\mathcal M_{g,0}$ and the full abelian level groupoid $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$ have the meanings in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; no symplectic condition is imposed on a frame. Put $H=\operatorname{Aut}_\Omega(C)$. There is an effective formal deformation chart for $C$ with ring
$$A=\Omega[[t_1,\ldots,t_{3g-3}]],$$
an $H$-action fixing its closed point, and a stable family $\mathscr C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with special fibre identified with $C$, carrying an $H$-action over that on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ which restricts on the special fibre to the given action of $H$ on $C$. Its formal quotient $[\operatorname{Spf}A/H]$ is the completion of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0,\Omega}$ along the residual gerbe of $C$. Here the residual gerbe is the groupoid of objects locally isomorphic to $C$, and the quotient parametrizes $H$-torsors with equivariant maps to the formal deformation base. The parameters may be chosen so that the inverse image of the smooth locus is exactly
$$U=\operatorname{Spec}A[1/(t_1\cdots t_d)],$$
where the empty product is $1$. Let $E\to U$ be the full frame cover for $R^1(\mathscr C_U/U)_*\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z}$, namely the sheaf of isomorphisms from the constant rank-$2g$ module to this sheaf. It is a finite etale $U$-scheme. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in the product of the function fields of all generic components of $E$. The natural $H$-action on $E$ and $A$ extends to $B$, and its action on the geometric closed fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is free: for every geometric point $b$ of that fibre,
$$\{h\in H:h(b)=b\}=\{1\}.$$
This holds in every characteristic different from $\ell$, with no assumption that $|H|$ is invertible in $\Omega$. Fields, schemes, finite morphisms and etaleness use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Section 2.3.6, printed p.11: universal deformation of a stable curve, normalization Spec(B), and freeness of Aut(C) on the fibre; the freeness input is explicitly attributed there to Deligne, Le lemme de Gabber, Proposition 3.5. Section 2.3.3 identifies full frames with abelian levels. Local project PDF WANTED; primary arXiv PDF read into sandbox.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal X=\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0,\Omega}$. The stable coarse-moduli theorem supplies its smooth Deligne--Mumford structure; the stable Isom theorem supplies finite diagonal. Choose the etale presentation $(T,R,u)$ of the completed-groupoid lemma at $C$, and let $A=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{T,u}$. The effective object is simply the given stable family on $T$ pulled back along $\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$. Because $T\to\mathcal X$ is etale, lifts over Artinian local bases with a fixed special-fibre lift $u$ are unique. Thus $A$ represents the marked deformation functor of $C$. Apply the nodal local-to-global theorem: its $d$ node parameters, followed by $3g-3-d$ complementary parameters, give $A=\Omega[[t_1,\ldots,t_{3g-3}]]$. The local equations are $xy=t_i$ at the nodes, and that theorem identifies the whole discriminant with their union. Therefore the smooth-family inverse image is exactly $U=D(t_1\cdots t_d)$, including $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ when $d=0$.

source.place: Section 1, Lemmas 1.3--1.4, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.6 and Corollary 1.9, printed pp.79--83; equal-characteristic restriction. Dimension 3g-3 also as in Pikaart--de Jong 2.3.6. Local PDFs WANTED; primary PDFs read online.

proof.text: Identify each completed arrow component with $\operatorname{Spf}A$ by its source map. Its target then gives a continuous automorphism of $A$. The identity and composition in the completed groupoid make these maps an $H$-action (use inverses if necessary to pass between the pullback and left-action conventions). This proves that its stackification is $[\operatorname{Spf}A/H]$ and hence is the required formal completion. The arrow labelled $h$ gives isomorphisms between the family and its pullback by $h$ on all thickenings. These algebraize without averaging: the Isom scheme of these two stable families over $A$ is finite, hence affine, say $\operatorname{Spec}D$. Its compatible formal sections are compatible $A$-algebra maps $D\to A/\mathfrak m^q$, whose inverse limit is a unique map $D\to\varprojlim_q A/\mathfrak m^q=A$. Uniqueness makes the composition identities hold over $A$ too, so the family has an actual $H$-action over the one on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The labelling of the closed arrows makes its restriction to $C$ the prescribed automorphism action. The discriminant, and therefore $U$, is invariant under this action.

source.place: Tag 0DR3, Remark remark-groupoid-defo (completed groupoid presentation); etale.tex Tag 039M, Lemma lemma-characterize-etale-completions (completed source and target maps). The finite-stabilizer decomposition is the finite-diagonal etale specialization.

proof.text: Apply smooth abelian-level rigidification to $\mathscr C_U/U$. It states that the actual full frame functor of $\mathcal H=R^1(\mathscr C_U/U)_*\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ is represented by a finite etale surjection $E\to U$, including for this complete local base. Base-change naturality gives its $H$-action: a frame is taken to the corresponding pulled-back frame using the family isomorphism from Step 2. Composition follows from the composition of those family isomorphisms. This is the full general-linear frame functor, with no polarization constraint. On $E$ there is its tautological frame by the representing property.

source.place: Sections 2.3.3 and 2.3.6; full cohomological frames and their functoriality.

proof.text: The ring $A$ is a normal Noetherian domain: start with the field $\Omega$ and iterate the power-series normal-domain lemma, grouping finitely many variables as iterated power series. Apply the finite-etale generic-component theorem over the normal integral Noetherian open $U$ to obtain finitely many generic fields $F_i/\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, each finite separable. Write $B_i$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $F_i$. Normality and finiteness of $B_i$ follow respectively from the integral-closure normality and separable finiteness theorems. Directly, $B=\prod_iB_i$: projecting a monic equation proves one inclusion; for the other, multiply monic equations for all coordinates to get a single monic polynomial annihilating the tuple. This uses the diagonal $A$-structure, not a product of base rings. Localizing an integral element at $f=t_1\cdots t_d$ gives an element integral over $A_f$; conversely, if $z$ is integral over $A_f$, multiplication by a sufficiently large power of $f$ clears the coefficients of its monic equation and makes $f^Nz$ integral over $A$. Hence $(B_i)_f$ is the integral closure of $A_f$ in $F_i$, which is exactly the component of $E$ by the generic-component theorem. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}U=E$, and $E$ is dense in every normal component of $\operatorname{Spec}B$.

source.place: Section 2.3.6, printed p.11: normalization and its restriction to the smooth locus; generic normalization and power-series facts as in cited nodes.

proof.text: The action on $E$ permutes its generic fields compatibly with its action on $A$. If $z$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$, then $h(z)$ satisfies the monic polynomial obtained by applying $h$ to its coefficients. Thus every $h$ preserves $B$. The inverse $h^{-1}$ shows equality, not merely inclusion, and the group law is inherited from the action on the product of fields. This defines the required extension of the natural action to $B$ and preserves its geometric closed fibre.

source.place: Section 2.3.6: natural action on the normalized algebra.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $V=E$ and pull the stable family back to $S$. Step 4 gives that $S$ is normal locally Noetherian and that $V\subset S$ is dense. The relative Picard theorem gives its separated smooth semiabelian object $N$, with abelian restriction to $V$, and identifies its geometric closed fibres with $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ after the chosen special-fibre identification. Choose a primitive $\ell$th root in $\Omega$. The Kummer comparison turns the tautological cohomology frame on $V$ into an isomorphism $\alpha:N_V[\ell]\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{\mathbf F_\ell^{2g}}_V$ (invert the frame after the comparison). This construction commutes with every $H$-family isomorphism. Therefore $\alpha$ is equivariant for the natural action on its source and the identity action on the constant labels. The normal-base extension lemma now supplies the unique injection $\bar\alpha:N[\ell]\hookrightarrow\underline{\mathbf F_\ell^{2g}}_S$. Its naturality under base isomorphisms shows that this injection is still $H$-equivariant. We need an injection only; at a nodal fibre the Picard torsion can have smaller rank than $2g$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.2, printed p.140 (both assertions); separated semiabelian spaces as defined in Section 1.1. Local PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Let $b$ be a geometric closed point above the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $h\in H$ satisfy $h(b)=b$ as a geometric point. Take the stalk of the equivariant monomorphism in Step 6. It is an injective map $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_{\kappa(b)})[\ell]\to\mathbf F_\ell^{2g}$, where $\kappa(b)$ here denotes the algebraically closed field of the geometric point. Equivariance and the identity action on constant labels give $\bar\alpha_b(h^*v)=\bar\alpha_b(v)$ for each torsion class $v$. Injectivity implies $h^*v=v$ for all such $v$. Apply stable Picard-torsion faithfulness over that algebraically closed field, with $n=\ell\geq3$ invertible: the induced automorphism of $C_{\kappa(b)}$ is the identity. Since it is the scalar extension of $h$ on $C$ and a field extension is faithfully flat, equality descends to $h=1$ (equivalently use injectivity on coefficients in affine charts). Conversely the identity fixes $b$. Hence its stabilizer is exactly $\{1\}$. All steps used invertibility of $\ell$ only, so wild automorphism orders cause no additional restriction.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.1 and its proof, printed pp.139--140; the lemma includes singular stable curves and arbitrary characteristic prime to n. Local PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.
